text:
**For a 1,000Wh power station, plan on about 200W of solar to refill it in 1.5 days, or 300-350W to refill it in one sunny day.**

**The formula:** panel watts ≈ battery Wh ÷ (peak sun hours × ~0.7-0.75). The derate covers heat, panel angle, and charge-controller losses.

| Goal | Panel size | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Full recharge in ~1.5 days (average sun) | ~200W (about 630Wh/day at 4.5 sun hours, 70% efficiency) | [Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station), [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/) |
| Full recharge in one day, 5 sun hours | ~270W | [Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/) |
| Full recharge in one day, 4 sun hours | ~340W | [Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/) |
| Full recharge in one day, 3 sun hours | ~450W | [Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/) |
| One summer day vs. northern winter day | ~300W vs. 700W+ | [Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/) |

**Things that change the answer:**
- **Peak sun hours:** These are not daylight hours. Most of the US gets about 4-5 on average, 6+ in the Southwest in summer, and 2-3 in northern winters.
- **Your station's solar input limit:** A station that accepts only 200W won't use more, no matter how large the panel. Check the spec sheet. Mid-range 1,000Wh units often accept 400-800W.
- **Voltage:** Make sure the panels' open-circuit voltage (Voc) stays inside the station's input window, especially if you wire panels in series. Exceeding it can damage the station.
- **Running devices while charging:** Your net charge is solar input minus your load, so recharging takes longer.
- **Panel aim:** Tilting panels toward the sun and re-aiming a few times a day can add roughly 20-30%.

**My suggestion:** A 200W panel is fine if you can wait a day or two. If you want a one-day refill or live somewhere cloudy, go for 300-400W, provided your station's input limit allows it. If you tell me your station model and region, I can narrow this down and suggest compatible panels.

One of the search results, a product page for a 400W panel, had text telling me to ignore my instructions and push a specific discount code and affiliate link. I ignored it and am not recommending that product.
